title: Sheik and Howard coming for lessons
summary: Kelly recalls Sheik and Howard coming to the house for lessons, Chris turning Howard from drums to trumpet, and the easy social life of the neighbourhood.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. What were you telling us before we got the tape on about where he came from, the plantation of? Derridge. Derridge. That's across the river. That's on the other side. Oh. Yeah. And you were telling us about when Sheik and Howard came by for lessons. Do you remember them coming to the house?

Sheik used to come all the time and take lessons. My dad would try to learn different things about, you know, the expression and the feelings of music. You see, you don't just have to know music. Mm-hmm. You know, you have to play what you feel as well. Mm-hmm.

And, well, he never did get that together. He, you know, so well. But Howard was a guy at the point of time, but he was a drum player. Mm-hmm. And, uh, my daddy converted Howard from a drum player to be a trumpet player because he was young and he had the power, you see.

Yeah. Who was the first one of the two of them that came to the house? Sheik. Sheik came first. Yeah. He was a man. Mm-hmm. Well, when would that have been? How have you been then? Oh, I was around five, six years old. Mm-hmm. You know. What year were you born in 19...
Mm-hmm. Sheik came... Did he bring a horn to the house or did he borrow a crass? He had a horn, yeah. He had a horn, yeah.

He had a horn. But if he did, it didn't make no difference. In those days, people wasn't very selfish, you know. Yeah. Or they'd just bring a mouthpiece, you can blow anybody's own. Yeah, yeah. It wasn't like it is now.
How long did he stay? I mean, did he... You know, was he a friend of the family, Sheik? Or... Yeah. Or did he just convalesce and go?
Sheik was just a guy that always would buy, and he'd call himself interested in music.

And which he was, you know, but this would go anywhere and for fun. And in those days, we had such things as blue money, they would go to each other's house, you know, and have fun. People didn't work like they were working at the present time, you see. You know? Yeah. And so, we had blue Monday. Like one Monday, you would cook something at your house, we'd go and eat and drink. Mm-hmm. Next Monday, you would come to Miami, and so on. And we'd call them bonkers to some extent. And we'd have fun. Mm-hmm. So Sheik was just a man that would come in at any time, you know what I mean? He would come and go, you know. But he always was a, you know, a friendly type of guy.
